knowledge:
- key_parameters: cores=Specifies the number of processor cores to use for parallel computing in read_coverage_batch and degnorm ;; iteration=Specifies the number of outer loops in the DegNorm algorithm (typically 5 is sufficient) ;; down_sampling=Set to 1 to bin read coverage scores by grid_size for baseline selection to improve efficiency, or 0 to disable downsampling ;; grid_size=Bin size in base pairs for downsampling (default is 10 bp, recommended to be less than 50 bp; ignored if down_sampling=0) ;; loop=Specifies the iteration number in the matrix factorization over-approximation (default is 100)
- alternatives: Global degradation normalization approaches (which apply a single normalization factor to all genes within a sample, failing to account for gene-specific degradation rates) ;; DegNorm independent Python package (the R Bioconductor package is recommended for the most updated version)
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing bulk RNA-seq data where samples exhibit varying degrees of RNA degradation, particularly because longer genes degrade faster than shorter ones, and you want to obtain unbiased read counts for differential expression analysis (e.g., with DESeq2 or edgeR).
- pitfalls: Genes with extremely low read counts (where more than half of the samples have less than 5 read counts) are filtered out and not normalized ;; The pipeline is highly computing-intensive and can take several hours; it is recommended to run it on high-performance servers or computing clusters rather than personal computers ;; In DegNorm versions prior to 1.3.1, a bug in the scaling factor determination using genes with maximum rho < 0.1 could return NA for datasets with many samples and large degradation.

workflows.name: degradation_normalization_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform degradation normalization on bulk RNA-seq BAM files using a GTF annotation to obtain degradation-normalized read counts and visualize degradation indices.
input: bam_files (RNA-seq alignment files in BAM format)
gtf_file (genome annotation file in GTF format)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify and list BAM and GTF files ;; 2. Calculate read coverage scores and counts across samples using read_coverage_batch ;; 3. Run the DegNorm core algorithm using degnorm to estimate degradation indices and normalize counts ;; 4. Visualize coverage curves, degradation index boxplots, heatmaps, and correlation matrices using plot_coverage, plot_boxplot, plot_heatmap, and plot_corr.
workflows.code:
bam_file_list=list.files(path=system.file("extdata",package="DegNorm"),
                        pattern=".bam$",full.names=TRUE)

gtf_file=list.files(path=system.file("extdata",package="DegNorm"),
                    pattern=".gtf$",full.names=TRUE)

coverage_res_chr21_sub=read_coverage_batch(bam_file_list, gtf_file,cores=2)

data("coverage_res_chr21")

summary_CoverageClass(coverage_res_chr21)

coverage_matrix=coverage_res_chr21$coverage
counts=coverage_res_chr21$counts

res_DegNorm_chr21 = degnorm(read_coverage = coverage_res_chr21[[1]],
                    counts = coverage_res_chr21[[2]],
                    iteration = 5,
                    down_sampling = 1,
                    grid_size=10,
                    loop = 100,
                    cores=2)

data("res_DegNorm_chr21")

summary_DegNormClass(res_DegNorm_chr21)

counts_normed=res_DegNorm_chr21$counts_normed

plot_coverage(gene_name="SOD1", coverage_output=coverage_res_chr21, 
            degnorm_output=res_DegNorm_chr21,group=c(0,1,1))

plot_coverage(gene_name="SOD1", coverage_output=coverage_res_chr21, 
            degnorm_output=res_DegNorm_chr21,group=c(0,1), 
            samples=c("SRR873822_chr21.bam", "SRR873834_chr21.bam"))

plot_boxplot(DI=res_DegNorm_chr21$DI)

plot_heatmap(DI=res_DegNorm_chr21$DI)

plot_corr(DI=res_DegNorm_chr21$DI)
